headline: Renewable resources replenish themselves—what you use today can grow back for tomorrow
universal_truth: Sustainable systems take only what regenerates; draw from the flow, not the stock
fun_facts: Forests can regenerate in 20-100 years if left alone—they're renewable on human timescales
The sun delivers more energy to Earth in one hour than humanity uses in a year
Fish populations can double in 1-14 years depending on species—if fishing doesn't exceed reproduction
discussion_questions: What in your life is renewable—regenerates after use?
What are you depleting faster than it replenishes?
How do you ensure sustainable 'harvesting' of your resources?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Cut a tree, plant a tree—in 50 years, you have another tree. Sunlight arrives fresh every day. Wind keeps blowing. Rain keeps falling. These are renewable resources: they replenish themselves. Use them wisely, and they last forever.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Some resources regenerate; others don't. This distinction is fundamental to sustainability. What makes something renewable?

options.text: Renewable resources regenerate on useful timescales—you can sustainably harvest if you take less than the replenishment rate; the flow continues indefinitely
options.response: Yes. The key is rate—take only what regenerates, and supply is unlimited. Exceed regeneration rate, and even renewable resources deplete. Sustainability is about matching extraction to replenishment.

options.text: Renewable just means it comes back
options.response: Comes back, yes, but the rate matters—overharvest and it won't return fast enough...

q1.title: Rate Matters
q1.script: Renewable doesn't mean infinite. Fish are renewable, but overfishing depletes them. Forests regrow, but clearing faster than growth creates deserts. Sustainability requires respecting regeneration rates.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Rate Matters"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Flow vs Stock
q2.script: Think in terms of flow versus stock. Flow is what regenerates continuously—like sunlight or interest. Stock is accumulated reserve. Sustainable living draws from flow, not stock.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Renewables
q3.script: You have renewable resources too: energy regenerates with rest, relationships with attention, skills with practice. But deplete faster than they regenerate, and even these run down.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Sustainable systems take only what regenerates. Draw from the flow, not the stock. Match consumption to replenishment.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 271. Tomorrow, we'll explore things that run out—non-renewable resources. Until then, identify what in your life is renewable.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Renewal Audit - What Regenerates?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify renewable resources and sustainable use rates
growTrack.activity: What resources do you use that regenerate—energy, time, relationships, money? Are you using them sustainably—at or below the regeneration rate? Where are you overdrawing? Adjust to sustainable levels.
